\chapter{Complexity — Oracle}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Oracle
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module defines oracle Turing machines in the sense of Arora--Barak
(Definition~3.4): multi-tape machines with one designated query tape and three
designated states, where entering the query state submits the query tape's
contents to an oracle language and moves, in a single step, to a positive- or
negative-answer state.  It provides the step and run semantics relative to an
oracle, a time-bounded computation predicate, basic locality invariants of
initialized runs (head positions and blank cells, bounding the query length),
and two lockstep sanity checks for the architecture: every plain machine embeds
as an oracle machine whose behavior is oracle-independent, and conversely every
oracle machine run with the empty oracle is eliminated into a plain machine.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Oracle Turing machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM}
\label{Turing.OracleTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
An oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes over a symbol alphabet
$\Sigma$ and state set $Q$ consists of an initial state $q_0$, a designated
query state $q_{\mathrm{query}}$, a designated positive-answer state
$q_{\mathrm{yes}}$, a designated negative-answer state $q_{\mathrm{no}}$, and a
transition function that assigns to every state, scanned input symbol
(possibly blank), and family of scanned symbols on the $k+1$ work tapes (the
last of which serves as the query tape) a one-step action on the $k+1$ work
tapes.  The transition function governs every state except the query state,
whose behavior is instead determined by the oracle.  The structure itself does
not require the three special states to be distinct; that is imposed
separately by well-formedness.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Well-formed oracle machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.WellFormed}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.WellFormed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM}
An oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes is well formed when its
three special states are pairwise distinct: the query state differs from the
positive-answer state, the query state differs from the negative-answer state,
and the two answer states differ from each other.  The initial state is
allowed to coincide with the query state (such a machine submits the empty
query on its first step).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Index of the query tape]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx}
\leanok
For an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, the index of the query
tape among the $k+1$ work tapes: the last index, $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Query string of a configuration]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queryString}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queryString}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx}
For a configuration of a machine with $k+1$ work tapes over an alphabet
$\Sigma$, the query string is the word read off the query tape (the last work
tape) from cell $0$ rightward, up to but excluding the first blank cell.  If
no cell at a nonnegative position of the query tape is blank --- possible for
an arbitrary configuration, though not for one reachable from an initial
configuration --- the query string is defined to be the empty word.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One step relative to an oracle]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.queryString}
One step of an oracle machine $M$ with $k$ ordinary work tapes relative to an
oracle language $O$ over the alphabet $\Sigma$, acting on a configuration $c$
with $k+1$ work tapes.  A halted configuration is left fixed.  If the current
state is the query state, the machine moves to the positive-answer state when
the query string of $c$ belongs to $O$ and to the negative-answer state
otherwise, with all tapes, head positions, and the output left unchanged.  In
every other state, the machine applies the action prescribed by its transition
function for the current state and the scanned input and work-tape symbols,
exactly like a plain multi-tape machine.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial configuration of an oracle machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.initCfg}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.initCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.OracleTM}
The initial configuration of an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes on
a given input word: the machine is in its initial state, the input head is at
the origin, all $k+1$ work tapes (including the query tape) are blank with
their heads at the origin, and the output is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Run of an oracle machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.step}
The configuration reached by running an oracle machine $M$ with oracle $O$ for
$t$ steps from a configuration $c$: the $t$-fold iterate of the one-step
function of $M$ relative to $O$, applied to $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Time-bounded oracle computation]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom}
An oracle machine $M$ with oracle $O$ computes the word $y$ on input $x$
within $t$ steps when, after running $M$ relative to $O$ for $t$ steps from
its initial configuration on $x$, the machine has halted and its output tape
holds exactly $y$.  This is a time-only notion; space is not constrained.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle-independence away from the query state]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_ne_qQuery}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_ne_qQuery}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes and let $c$ be a
configuration whose current state is not the query state of $M$ (in
particular, $c$ may be halted).  Then for any two oracle languages $O_1$ and
$O_2$, one step of $M$ from $c$ relative to $O_1$ equals one step of $M$ from
$c$ relative to $O_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Actions write only under the head]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.apply_workTapes_eq_of_ne}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.apply_workTapes_eq_of_ne}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $a$ be a one-step action of a machine with $k'$ work tapes, let $c$ be a
configuration of such a machine, let $i$ be a work-tape index, and let $z$ be
an integer cell position different from the position of the $i$-th work head
in $c$.  Then after applying $a$ to $c$, the content of cell $z$ of the $i$-th
work tape is unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Heads move at most one cell per oracle step]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.workTapePos_step_le}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.workTapePos_step_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.workTapePos_apply_le}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, $O$ an oracle
language, $c$ a configuration, and $i$ one of the $k+1$ work-tape indices.
Then the position of the $i$-th work head after one step of $M$ relative to
$O$ differs from its position in $c$ by at most $1$ in absolute value.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Oracle steps write only under the head]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.workTapes_step_eq_of_ne}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.workTapes_step_eq_of_ne}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.apply_workTapes_eq_of_ne, Turing.OracleTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, $O$ an oracle
language, $c$ a configuration, $i$ one of the $k+1$ work-tape indices, and $z$
an integer cell position different from the position of the $i$-th work head
in $c$.  Then after one step of $M$ relative to $O$, the content of cell $z$
of the $i$-th work tape is unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Locality invariant of an initialized oracle run]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_workTapes_invariant}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_workTapes_invariant}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.workTapePos_step_le, Turing.OracleTM.workTapes_step_eq_of_ne}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, $O$ an oracle
language, and $x$ an input word.  Then for every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, in the
configuration reached by running $M$ with oracle $O$ for $t$ steps from its
initial configuration on $x$: every one of the $k+1$ work heads is at a
position of absolute value at most $t$, and every work-tape cell at an integer
position $z$ with $t \le \abs{z}$ is blank.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Query length is bounded by the running time]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_workTapes_invariant}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, $O$ an oracle
language, $x$ an input word, and $t \in \mathbb{N}$.  In the configuration
reached by running $M$ with oracle $O$ for $t$ steps from its initial
configuration on $x$, the query string --- the contents of the query tape from
cell $0$ up to the first blank cell --- has length at most $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distant cells stay blank in an initialized run]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_workTapes_blank}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_workTapes_blank}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_workTapes_invariant}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, $O$ an oracle
language, $x$ an input word, and $t \in \mathbb{N}$.  Then in the
configuration reached by running $M$ with oracle $O$ for $t$ steps from its
initial configuration on $x$, every work-tape cell at an integer position $z$
with $t \le \abs{z}$ is blank.  In particular, the query tape always contains
a blank cell at a nonnegative position, so the empty-word fallback in the
definition of the query string is never invoked in an initialized run.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Extension of an action by an inert tape]
\lean{Turing.Action.extend}
\label{Turing.Action.extend}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
The extension of a one-step action on $k$ work tapes to an action on $k+1$
work tapes: on the first $k$ tapes it writes and moves exactly as before, and
on the extra last tape it writes nothing and does not move the head.  The
input-head move, the output emission, and the next state are unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Embedding of a configuration for the oracle model]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle}
\label{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
The embedding of a configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes and state
set $Q$ into a configuration of a machine with $k+1$ work tapes over the
extended state set $Q \sqcup \{0,1,2\}$: the state (if the machine has not
halted) is renamed along the left inclusion, the input head, the first $k$
work tapes with their head positions, and the output are unchanged, and the
extra last work tape is blank with its head at the origin.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Embedding preserves the scanned input symbol]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_inputSymbol}
\label{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_inputSymbol}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol}
\difficulty{1}
For any configuration $c$ of a machine with $k$ work tapes, the input symbol
scanned in the embedding of $c$ into the $(k+1)$-tape oracle model equals the
input symbol scanned in $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Embedding preserves the scanned work symbols]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_workTapeSymbols}
\label{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_workTapeSymbols}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols}
\difficulty{1}
For any configuration $c$ of a machine with $k$ work tapes and any of the $k$
original tape indices $i$, the symbol scanned on tape $i$ in the embedding of
$c$ into the $(k+1)$-tape oracle model equals the symbol scanned on tape $i$
in $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Embedding preserves haltedness]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_state_eq_none}
\label{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_state_eq_none}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle}
\difficulty{1}
A configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes is halted if and only if its
embedding into the $(k+1)$-tape oracle model is halted.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Embedding preserves the output]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_output}
\label{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_output}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle}
\difficulty{1}
For any configuration $c$ of a machine with $k$ work tapes, the output tape of
the embedding of $c$ into the $(k+1)$-tape oracle model equals the output tape
of $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Embedding commutes with applying an action]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_apply}
\label{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Action.extend, Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle}
\difficulty{4}
Let $a$ be a one-step action of a machine with $k$ work tapes and state set
$Q$, and let $c$ be a configuration of such a machine.  Rename the states of
$a$ along the left inclusion $Q \to Q \sqcup \{0,1,2\}$ and extend the result
by an inert $(k+1)$-st tape.  Applying this extended, renamed action to the
embedding of $c$ into the $(k+1)$-tape oracle model yields exactly the
embedding of the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Embedding sends initial configurations to initial configurations]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_init}
\label{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_init}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle, Turing.Cfg.init}
\difficulty{1}
For any state $q_0$ of a machine with $k$ work tapes and any input word $x$,
the embedding into the $(k+1)$-tape oracle model of the initial configuration
in state $q_0$ on input $x$ is the initial configuration on input $x$ whose
state is the image of $q_0$ under the left inclusion into the extended state
set $Q \sqcup \{0,1,2\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Plain machine as an oracle machine that never queries]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.extend, Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleTM}
The embedding of a plain multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes and state set
$Q$ as an oracle machine over the extended state set $Q \sqcup \{0,1,2\}$: the
three fresh states serve as the query, positive-answer, and negative-answer
states, the initial state is the image of the original initial state, and on
original states the transition function is the original transition (renamed
along the left inclusion and extended by an inert query tape), so that the
machine never moves into a fresh state and ignores the query tape.  From each
of the three fresh states the transition table halts immediately.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The embedded machine is well formed]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM_wellFormed}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM_wellFormed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleTM.WellFormed, Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM}
\difficulty{1}
For every plain multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes, the oracle machine
obtained by embedding it into the oracle model is well formed: its three fresh
special states (query, positive answer, negative answer) are pairwise
distinct.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[One step of an embedded plain machine]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step_ofMultiTapeTM}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.step_ofMultiTapeTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.extend, Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_apply, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_workTapeSymbols, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M_0$ be a plain multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes, let $O$ be any
oracle language, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M_0$.  One step, relative
to $O$, of the oracle machine obtained by embedding $M_0$, taken from the
embedding of $c$ into the $(k+1)$-tape oracle model, equals the embedding of
the configuration obtained by one step of $M_0$ from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[An embedded plain machine runs in lockstep]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_ofMultiTapeTM}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_ofMultiTapeTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.step_ofMultiTapeTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M_0$ be a plain multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes, let $O$ be any
oracle language, let $c$ be a configuration of $M_0$, and let
$t \in \mathbb{N}$.  Running the oracle machine obtained by embedding $M_0$
for $t$ steps relative to $O$ from the embedding of $c$ yields the embedding
of the configuration obtained by running $M_0$ for $t$ steps from $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Behavior of an embedded plain machine is oracle-independent]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.computesInTime_ofMultiTapeTM}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.computesInTime_ofMultiTapeTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.embedOracle, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_init, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_output, Turing.Cfg.embedOracle_state_eq_none, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.ofMultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_ofMultiTapeTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M_0$ be a plain multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes, let $O$ be any
oracle language, let $x$ and $y$ be words, and let $t \in \mathbb{N}$.  The
oracle machine obtained by embedding $M_0$ computes $y$ on input $x$ within
$t$ steps relative to $O$ if and only if, after running $M_0$ for $t$ steps
from its initial configuration on $x$, the machine has halted and its output
tape holds exactly $y$.  In particular, the input/output behavior and time
bounds of the embedded machine do not depend on the oracle.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Empty-oracle elimination]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.OracleTM}
Given an oracle machine $M$ with $k$ ordinary work tapes and state set $Q$,
the plain multi-tape machine with $k+1$ work tapes over the same state set $Q$
that simulates $M$ run with the empty oracle: it has the same initial state,
and its transition function agrees with that of $M$ in every state except the
query state, where it instead performs a stationary move (no writes, no head
movement, no output) directly into the negative-answer state, since the empty
oracle always answers no.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One step of the empty-oracle elimination]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step_plainEmptyOracle}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.step_plainEmptyOracle}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle, Turing.OracleTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes and let $c$ be a
configuration with $k+1$ work tapes.  One step of the plain machine obtained
from $M$ by the empty-oracle elimination, taken from $c$, equals one step of
$M$ relative to the empty oracle, taken from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[The empty-oracle elimination runs in lockstep]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_plainEmptyOracle}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_plainEmptyOracle}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.step_plainEmptyOracle}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, let $c$ be a
configuration with $k+1$ work tapes, and let $t \in \mathbb{N}$.  Running the
plain machine obtained from $M$ by the empty-oracle elimination for $t$ steps
from $c$ yields exactly the configuration obtained by running $M$ for $t$
steps from $c$ relative to the empty oracle.
\end{theorem}
